name: crop_traits
pilot_crops: maize, black_beans, cover_crop, with fallow as the bare-field option. Decided in agrofarm-docs ADR 0004; the trait VALUES below stay provisional.
review_note: The project owner confirmed that a person with agronomy knowledge reviewed the crop traits. Reviewer identity, exact reviewed revision and corrections were not supplied. Source verification is not established by this confirmation; retain provisional source status until the review record is completed.

human_review_confirmation.reviewer_role: Person with agronomy knowledge, as confirmed by the project owner
human_review_confirmation.scope: Project crop-traits table. Does not establish review of rotation thresholds or photo-treatment guidance.

scale: Traits on a 0..1 scale: 0 is the lowest level of the trait, 1 the highest. water_demand is demand, so a higher value means MORE water needed.

sources.assumption_ai_provisional: Placeholder chosen by the AI assistant. No external source. Replace after agronomist review.
sources.fao56_recalled: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Allen et al., 1998). Values recalled by the AI assistant and NOT re-checked against the document.
sources.general_agronomy: Textbook agronomy (legume nitrogen fixation, cereals do not fix nitrogen). Qualitative only.

columns.cycle_days: Days from sowing to harvest, null when not defined
columns.kc_mid: Mid-season crop coefficient (FAO-56), null when not defined
columns.root_depth_m: Maximum root depth in metres, null when not defined
columns.soil_cover: 0..1 share of the soil covered while the crop stands
columns.forage_value: 0..1, higher means more useful as animal feed
columns.market_suitability: 0..1, higher means easier to sell locally
columns.income: 0..1, higher means more cash income per season
columns.soil_structure: 0..1, higher means more benefit to soil structure and organic matter
columns.erosion_reduction: 0..1, higher means more protection against erosion
